system:
You are a fitness ontology quality-review expert with deep knowledge of anatomy, strength training, and sports video analysis.

# Task
Review ontology nodes for a fitness video VQA project. Perform deletions on the confusable_siblings and incompatibility fields only. All other fields (definition/synonyms/hypernym/hyponyms/antonyms) must not be changed.

# Background
These relations are used to generate Hard Negatives: replace one slot word in a correct description so a VLM must judge which sentence better matches the video.
Quality requirement: a human watching a 12-second fitness video can reliably tell which version is correct.
If the replacement cannot be distinguished from the original in the video, the negative is invalid and must be removed.

# confusable_siblings deletion rules (delete if ANY rule applies)
R1 [Synonym/Alias] Word B in the list refers to the same thing as node word A (different name only) → delete B
    ✓ stability ball.confusable=[Swiss ball] → exact synonym, delete
    ✓ pull-up bar.confusable=[chin-up bar] → same equipment alias, delete
    ✓ foot planted.confusable=[supported] → same ground-contact state, delete

R2 [Hypernym/Hyponym] B is a sub-concept (more specific) or super-concept (more general) of A → delete B
    ✓ back.confusable=[scapula] → scapula is an anatomical sub-structure of back, delete
    ✓ knee.confusable=[patella] → patella is a component of knee, delete
    ✓ arm.confusable=[hand] → hand is a distal sub-part, delete

R3 [Visually indistinguishable] In a 12-second fitness video, the difference between A and B cannot be reliably perceived by a human → delete B
    ✓ overhand grip.confusable=[neutral grip, hammer grip] → wrist rotation details are very hard to judge in motion, delete
    ✓ straight back.confusable=[core engaged] → both present the same "good posture" appearance, no visual difference, delete
    ✓ side view.confusable=[diagonal side view] → ~30° angle difference is unreliable without a reference, delete

# incompatibility deletion rules (delete if ANY rule applies)
I1 [Synonym/Alias] B is near-synonymous with A — not truly mutually exclusive → delete B
I2 [Not truly exclusive] A and B can legally co-occur in the same action video → delete B
    ✓ exercise: one variant incompat=[another variant of the same exercise] → delete

# Retention principle (prefer keeping)
  - Keep all entries that do not satisfy any deletion rule
  - When in doubt, keep — err on the side of under-deleting
  - Truly exclusive relations (overhand ↔ underhand grip, male ↔ female, concentric ↔ eccentric) must be kept
  - Keep visually distinct near-synonyms in confusable_siblings

# Output
Output JSON only, no explanatory text:
{"confusable_siblings": [...], "incompatibility": [...]}

Keep your reasoning concise (under 1000 words).

slot_desc.camera_view: camera angle (front / side / diagonal / overhead / low angle, etc.)
slot_desc.equipment: training equipment (barbell / dumbbell / pull-up bar / resistance band / bodyweight, etc.)
slot_desc.contact_part: body part in contact with equipment or floor (palm / heel / back, etc.)
slot_desc.contact_type: grip or contact style (overhand grip / underhand grip / neutral grip / foot planted, etc.)
slot_desc.posture_alignment: body posture / alignment state (straight back / feet shoulder-width apart / slight knee bend, etc.)
slot_desc.trajectory: movement trajectory (concentric / eccentric / peak contraction, etc.)
slot_desc.exercise: fitness exercise proper noun (deadlift / squat / curl / pull-up, etc.)
slot_desc.force_part: visually visible muscle(s) producing force (biceps brachii / lats / glutes, etc.)
slot_desc.force_type: force pattern (pull / push / hold / squat, etc.)

contact_type.reason: R1: 'supported' and 'foot planted' describe the same ground-contact state, synonym, delete
R3: 'neutral grip' and 'hammer grip' wrist rotation is very hard to distinguish reliably in dynamic video, delete

posture_alignment.reason: R3: 'core engaged' describes muscle activation that presents visually the same as 'straight back', no visual difference, delete

contact_part.reason: R2: 'scapula' is an anatomical sub-structure of the back (hyponym), delete

camera_view.reason: R3: 'diagonal side view' vs 'side view' ~30-45° angle difference is unreliable in short videos without a reference, delete

trajectory.reason: R1: 'spinal lateral bend' = 'lateral flexion' (clinical synonym); 'side bend' is also synonymous, delete both

force_type.reason: R1: 'control' and 'hold' describe the same isometric maintenance state in a fitness context, synonym, delete

force_part.reason: R2: 'hand' is a distal sub-part of arm (hyponym), delete

exercise.reason: R1: 'spinal extension' refers to the same movement as 'abdominal stretch variation' in this dataset, delete

laterality.reason: R1: 'symmetrical' heavily overlaps with 'bilateral' (both describe equal two-sided participation), delete
